title: Health & pharmacy
body:
No vaccines are required for entry. The CDC recommends being current on routine shots (MMR, Tdap, flu) plus hepatitis A and B for most travelers; yellow fever is not recommended for Uruguay itself. Tap water is generally safe to drink in Montevideo and the other cities on this trip.

Pharmacies ("farmacias") are common and well-stocked in all three towns; look for a green cross sign. Farmashop and San Roque are the widest chains.

title: Emergency numbers
body:
Dial 911 nationwide for police, or the direct lines: police 911, medical/ambulance 105, fire 104. Uruguay's Ministry of Tourism runs a free non-emergency tourist helpline at 0800-8748 (business hours) for scams, lost documents, and general hassles. Seasonal tourist police patrol Ciudad Vieja in Montevideo and Colonia's historic quarter during summer, with some English.

⚠ The US State Department's advisory is unconfirmed (see the Plan tab) — check it directly before travel. As general practice in crowded tourist spots (Mercado del Puerto, Carnival crowds, the Rambla at night), keep phones and bags zipped and front-facing; petty theft is the more common tourist-facing risk than violent crime, but confirm current specifics against the advisory itself.
